scenes.headline: How a flow map learns to follow the noise
scenes.sub: Improved training of strong stochastic flow maps
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Transom! A stochastic flow map jumps a noisy process forward in a few big steps. Here's how it got the best training loss.

scenes.text: Swap the rough Brownian path for a smooth polynomial that converges to it, so the map can be trained with a derivative loss.
scenes.say: Brownian motion has no slope anywhere. So replace it with a smooth polynomial that converges to it, and train against that.

scenes.title: Two ways to train the map

left.title: Semigroup loss
items: One big step equals two halves
Needs no derivative of the path
left.say: The first paper used a semigroup loss. One big step must equal two half steps. No derivative needed.

right.title: Wong-Zakai loss
items: The polynomial path has a slope
Train the random ODE's flow map
right.say: The new paper trains the flow map of a random ordinary differential equation. Its slope exists, and every coefficient enters the loss.

scenes.title: The random ODE
scenes.say: Here is the equation the map now learns.

parts.note: the drift of the original stochastic equation
parts.say: The first term is the usual drift.

parts.note: slope of the Legendre polynomial of the path
parts.say: The second is the slope of the polynomial path. As the degree grows, the solution converges to the true stochastic one.

scenes.title: One step of the improved map

steps.say: Summarise the noise on the step as three Legendre coefficients.
They enter a pretrained flow model through a residual that starts at zero, so the model begins as its teacher.
The noise term is computed exactly, from the same path, not learned by a head.
Drift plus exact noise gives the next state, in one network call.
Top, the smooth path, where a derivative loss exists. Bottom, the rough path, where only the semigroup loss works.
On ImageNet, the improved map sits below the original at every step count.

scenes.title: FD-DINOv2 at 4 steps, lower is better
scenes.note: against the authors' own port of SSFM
scenes.say: At four steps, the new parameterisation and the new loss each roughly halve the error, against the authors' own port of the original.

scenes.text: Turn the noise into an input the derivative can see, and a stochastic map trains like a deterministic one.
scenes.mark: an input the derivative can see
scenes.say: Turn the noise into an input the derivative can see, and a stochastic map trains like a deterministic one.

recap: Smooth polynomial stands in for the path
Derivative loss on the random ODE
scenes.say: A polynomial path, a derivative loss, and exact noise. That's the improved strong flow map.
